sec: Type 1 DM pathophysiology and Type 1 versus Type 2

items.q: The pathophysiology line for Type 1 DM describes T-cell-mediated destruction of the:
items.exp: The page writes T-cell-mediated beta-cell destruction with insulinitis. (Book p923)

items.q: Match the Type 1 versus Type 2 factor to the printed pair — 1) Age 2) Weight 3) Family history 4) DKA … A) Younger / older B) Thinner / obese C) Rare / common D) Common / rare
items.exp: The comparison table lists younger versus older age, thinner versus obese weight, rare versus common family history, and common versus rare DKA for Type 1 versus Type 2. (Book p923)

items.q: Assess the marker line: I GAD and ZnT-8 are listed among Type 1 markers. II Anti-insulin antibody is absent from the marker line.
items.exp: The marker line includes GAD, ZnT-8 and anti-insulin antibody. (Book p923)

items.q: What Type 1 twin-to-twin concordance is written in the final row?
items.exp: The Type 1 column gives twin-to-twin concordance as 40%. (Book p923)

items.q: The HLA association line shows positive association with DR3–DR___ in the Type 1 note.
items.exp: The HLA association diagram shows positive DR3–DR4 and a negative DR1–14 entry. (Book p923)

items.q: A patient has osmotic symptoms, low C-peptide and common DKA. Which column in the comparison table fits best?
items.exp: Osmotic symptoms, low C-peptide and common DKA are entries in the Type 1 DM column. (Book p923)

items.q: Match the comparison factor to the Type 1 entry — 1) C-peptide 2) Acanthosis nigricans 3) Dyslipidemia 4) Antibodies … A) Low B) Absent C) Absent D) Present
items.exp: The Type 1 column gives low C-peptide, absent acanthosis nigricans, absent dyslipidemia and present antibodies. (Book p923)

items.q: Assess the endocrine-association rows: I PCOS is rare in the Type 1 column and present in Type 2. II HLA association is stronger in Type 1 than Type 2.
items.exp: The table marks PCOS rare/present and HLA association stronger/weaker for Type 1/Type 2. (Book p923)

items.q: If both parents have DM, what risks are printed for Type 1 and Type 2 respectively?
items.exp: The risk rows state 15% for Type 1 and 40% for Type 2 when both parents have DM. (Book p923)

items.q: Which Type 1 versus Type 2 factor is labelled stronger for Type 2?
items.exp: The final comparison rows mark genetic-factor association as weaker in Type 1 and stronger in Type 2. (Book p923)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the Type 2 entries in the comparison table?
items.exp: The Type 2 antibody entry is absent; older age, higher C-peptide and present acanthosis nigricans are listed. (Book p923)

items.q: A family-risk question asks about one parent having DM. Which Type 1/Type 2 risk pair is printed?
items.exp: The row for either parent having DM gives 5% for Type 1 and 25% for Type 2. (Book p923)
